Our history teacher tried something different today. Instead of lecturing on Partition she split us into groups and gave each group a different first-hand account: a refugee family, a train guard, a soldier, a kid our age.

We had to read ours out loud. The kid's one was the worst. He talks about hiding in a sugarcane field for two days while his village was attacked, and he's so matter of fact about it.

Nobody joked around for the rest of the period. I think it's the first time history felt like it happened to actual people. Do other schools do stuff like this or did we just get lucky with our teacher?
